### 2026-10-06 – oct. 5-6: First concepts of "Parrot"

**1.5h**

oct. 5-6: First concepts of "Parrot"

INTRODUCTION (Hello World:D)
Hello guys this is my first journal about my project of designing and building a small helper bot called "Parrot".
A assistant that can help me with completing various trivia tasks.

WHY AM I BUILDING THIS?
I am really not happy with the effectiveness of my workflow and I wanted to change that for a while now. The solution to this problem is a little helper, that can do tasks for me whilst im working. It is a bit like an AI Agent but hell not as advanced. The main focus lies on hardware help but also in the software area it could be of some help.

oct. 6

CORE CONCEPT
Before we continue, I want to explain in more detail the idea of the project and its core features.

As already stated above, i want to create a little assistant to help with my work. For simplification and to make the project not so big and beginner friendly, I am going to start with the brain of the bot and its senses. But it will also receive an extension port. What is this you may ask. Its the key to his mobility and the potential of the project to accomplish different tasks. With it, it can for example connect to a vehicle to move around or perhaps to a robotic arm to clean up my workspace.

The Core idea is to create a modular project with the potential to becoming a great project but also being beginner friendly and simple at the beginning.

### 2026-10-07 – oct. 7: Idea and plan are ready now !

**6h**

oct. 7: Idea and plan are ready now !

INTRODUCTION

Hey guys, today has been a productive day and lots of stuff has been done. The general Concept is done and all questions for the project have been answered.

After some consideration and some thinking i first settled on a quite advanced project with a size that wasnt exactly ideal for my skills (and for the budget :X ). After some more brainstorming i settled with a more minimal version that still represents all my ideas in an optimal way.

This results in the following situation. Im going to concentrate on a minimal version first and add more features and pcb designs after the initial version is done. Lets see how far I will get XD.

TABLE OF CONTENT

oct. 7
- Brainstorming of the final idea.
- yet another rough PCB layout. (certainly not the last)
- power distribution on the board and the extension Ports
- Pin mapout of the ESP and rough connection to the other parts
- (i also did a rough BOM already but nooot done yet)

THE IDEA   :O

Well where do i start, probably with a short summary of the end status.
The project will be a brain (central control board) for a small helper Bot. This Brain PCB consists of an ESP32, an IMU and some magic extension ports. These extension ports are the interesting part. They make it possible for extensions to be plugged into the Brain.

So far so good, but what extensions you might ask.
Primarily there will be a so called sense extensions (S1). This extension is different from other extensions and is responsible for all senses of the bot (mics, camera, display for expressions, etc.) The connector for this extension also is different from the other extension ports but ill get to this later.
Other extensions could be some for movement or for the ability of interaction (vehicle, legs, robo arm,etc.) They all have the same type of extension port.

This is the full idea but for this project there only will be one extension port and one S1 port, but this is still ok since there could also be extension extensions XD.

POWER DISTRIBUTION

The power distribution of the board is a bit more complicated. It is split in two sources. The Logic domain and the Extension power domain.
![ImageTemp 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wKsIODyJMOqccfQq70tFSoimsjj2E03H/3d504ed4a4ff0844f6d458615a1f35e22bf874d0dc073a99113a50a11282e2c4.jpg)
The Logic domain is powered by one onboard 1S LiPo battery (2000mAh prob.). It powers all the Brain components and keeps a konstant and safe power domain for all systems relevant parts on the board.

The  Extension power domain is powered by a external 2S LiPo battery (with more power than the onboard), connected via an XT30 connector on the board, to power the extension ports separately. The main idea behind this is, that the extensions probably need way more voltage than the Brain itself and its safer to split the power sources then.
